content.overview: A storage excursion or package failure should trigger evidence preservation and status control. Restoration of conditions does not by itself decide product consequence.

vocabulary.definition: Visible and recorded designation preventing material from moving outside its authorized state.
Departure from a defined environmental or process condition.
Comparison of expected and actual material identity, quantity, location and status.

sections.title: Preserve the exposure timeline
sections.body: Record when the event began, how it was detected, duration, locations, package conditions and actions taken.

sections.title: Scope lots and units
sections.body: Inventory and location records should identify which material shared the exposure without broadening or narrowing scope for convenience.

sections.title: Handoff status and evidence gaps
sections.body: Receiving roles need explicit holds, pending measurements, open decisions and accountable owners.

workedExamples: A cooler returns to setpoint after an alarm, but the affected lots remain on hold until exposure and product evidence are reviewed.
commonMistakes: Closing an event when equipment recovers.
Moving inventory without preserving original location.
Relying on label color without a controlled status record.
content.practicalApplication: Prepare a storage-excursion packet with timeline, inventory scope, package observations, measurements, status and next decision owner.
content.summary: Storage deviations are managed through traceable exposure evidence and lot-status control, not automatic release or rejection.
